key_insight: Early wall heat losses strongly reshape premixed flame acceleration in confined channels, promoting tulip flame formation and its distortion beyond the adiabatic case.
engineering_relevance: For safety-critical combustors and confined hydrogen systems, accurately accounting for wall thermal coupling is essential to predict flame evolution, pressure rise, and possible flame instabilities.
method: Direct numerical simulation of fully compressible reactive Navier–Stokes equations
Detailed chemical kinetics and transport for stoichiometric hydrogen–air mixtures
Conjugate heat transfer with conductive channel walls and outer-surface losses
evidence_signal: The simulations are compared against adiabatic-wall cases and reproduce the main experimentally observed features of flame dynamics in 2D and cylindrical channels.
watch_item: Results depend on detailed wall heat-transfer modeling and channel geometry, so predictive accuracy may change if wall properties, boundary conditions, or aspect ratio differ from the studied cases.
paper_title: The Effect of Heat Loss During the Early Stages of Flame Propagation and Tulip Flame Formation
